# pf_qos (Resource)

The firewall's QoS: HFSC queue trees and the `match` rules that classify traffic into them. There is **one QoS document per firewall**; declare at most one `pf_qos` per provider configuration.

pf only allows queues in the main ruleset, so pfapid applies a change by reloading the base ruleset (atomic; API anchors and table contents are kept). Changes use commit-confirm like `pf_anchor`, and `terraform plan` checks the queues and rules with `pfctl -n` against the firewall's real base ruleset.

Classify on the rule that **creates the state**: for a connection opened from outside, that is `direction = "in"`. pf then queues the replies that leave the firewall. A `match out` rule is never evaluated for packets of an existing state.

Creating this resource fails if the firewall already has a QoS document; import it with `terraform import <address> qos`. Destroying it removes all queues. The pfapid client needs the `qos` grant.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# One QoS configuration per firewall. The base ruleset must carry pfapid's
# QoS hooks, and vio1 must be in the firewall's policy.queue_interfaces.
resource "pf_qos" "fw" {
  queues = [
    { name = "rootq", interface = "vio1", bandwidth = "1G", max = "1G" },
    { name = "std", parent = "rootq", bandwidth = "800M", default = true },
    { name = "backup", parent = "rootq", bandwidth = "100M", max = "200M" },
    { name = "voip", parent = "rootq", bandwidth = "50M", flows = 1024, quantum = 1500 },
  ]

  rules = [
    # Classify where the state is created: connections come IN on frontend,
    # and pf queues the replies leaving the firewall.
    {
      direction = "in"
      interface = "frontend"
      family    = "inet"
      protocol  = "tcp"
      to        = { table = "backup_targets", ports = [{ from = 873 }] }
      queue     = { name = "backup" }
      label     = "qos-backup"
    },
    {
      direction = "in"
      interface = "frontend"
      family    = "inet6"
      protocol  = "udp"
      to        = { ports = [{ from = 5060, to = 5061 }] }
      queue     = { name = "voip", priority = "std" }
      prio      = { normal = 6 }
    },
  ]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `queues` (Attributes List) Queues, parents before children. Each physical interface has at most one tree, and each tree exactly one `default` leaf. Children may not add up to more than their parent's bandwidth. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--queues))
- `rules` (Attributes List) Classification rules (`match`), in order. Each sets `queue`, `prio` or both. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))

### Read-Only

- `etag` (String) Version of the committed QoS document.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `pf_rules` (List of String) Queues and rules as pf loads them (`pfctl -nv`). Computed at plan time.

<a id="nestedatt--queues"></a>
### Nested Schema for `queues`

Required:

- `bandwidth` (String) Target bandwidth. A bit rate: a number with an optional `K`, `M` or `G` suffix, e.g. `100M` (pf has no percentages).
- `name` (String) Queue name, unique on the firewall.

Optional:

- `default` (Boolean) The queue for traffic no rule classifies. Exactly one leaf per tree. Defaults to `false`.
- `flows` (Number) Make this leaf an FQ-CoDel queue with this many flows.
- `interface` (String) Root queues only: the physical interface (from the firewall's `policy.queue_interfaces`; not a group).
- `max` (String) Hard limit. A bit rate: a number with an optional `K`, `M` or `G` suffix, e.g. `100M` (pf has no percentages).
- `min` (String) Guaranteed minimum. A bit rate: a number with an optional `K`, `M` or `G` suffix, e.g. `100M` (pf has no percentages).
- `parent` (String) Every other queue: its parent queue.
- `qlimit` (Number) Packets the queue may hold.
- `quantum` (Number) FQ-CoDel quantum in bytes (flow queues only).


<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Required:

- `family` (String) `inet` or `inet6`.
- `interface` (String) Interface or group from the firewall's pfapid policy (e.g. `frontend`).

Optional:

- `direction` (String) `in` or `out`. Omit for both. See the note on states above.
- `from` (Attributes) Source. Omit for `any`. At most one of `prefixes`, `table`, `interface` and `self`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--from))
- `label` (String) pf label, shown in `pfctl -s labels` (letters, digits, space and `_.:/-`, at most 63).
- `log` (Boolean) Log matching packets to pflog. Defaults to `false`.
- `prio` (Attributes) Queue priority (`set prio`): `normal`, and optionally `low` for empty ACKs and low-delay packets. 0–7. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--prio))
- `protocol` (String) `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp` (inet) or `icmp6` (inet6). Omit for any.
- `queue` (Attributes) `set queue`: a leaf queue, and optionally a second one for low-delay packets and TCP ACKs. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--queue))
- `to` (Attributes) Destination. Omit for `any`. At most one of `prefixes`, `table`, `interface` and `self`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--to))

<a id="nestedatt--rules--from"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.from`

Optional:

- `interface` (String) The interface's own addresses, `(name)` in pf.
- `negate` (Boolean) Negate the address: `! <address>` in pf. Needs exactly one address: a single prefix, a table, an interface or `self`. A negated list is refused because pf expands `{ !a !b }` into rules that together match everything; negate a table instead. Defaults to `false`.
- `ports` (Attributes List) Ports (protocol `tcp` or `udp` only). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--from--ports))
- `prefixes` (List of String) Canonical CIDR prefixes, all of the rule's `family`.
- `self` (Boolean) Every address of the firewall itself: `self` in pf. Defaults to `false`.
- `table` (String) A table, `<table>` in pf: one pfapid manages (`policy.tables`) or one the base ruleset owns (`policy.ref_tables`, e.g. a `const` table).

<a id="nestedatt--rules--from--ports"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.from.ports`

Required:

- `from` (Number) Port, or first port of a range.

Optional:

- `to` (Number) Last port of the range (inclusive). Omit for a single port.



<a id="nestedatt--rules--prio"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.prio`

Required:

- `normal` (Number)

Optional:

- `low` (Number)


<a id="nestedatt--rules--queue"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.queue`

Required:

- `name` (String)

Optional:

- `priority` (String)


<a id="nestedatt--rules--to"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.to`

Optional:

- `interface` (String) The interface's own addresses, `(name)` in pf.
- `negate` (Boolean) Negate the address: `! <address>` in pf. Needs exactly one address: a single prefix, a table, an interface or `self`. A negated list is refused because pf expands `{ !a !b }` into rules that together match everything; negate a table instead. Defaults to `false`.
- `ports` (Attributes List) Ports (protocol `tcp` or `udp` only). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--to--ports))
- `prefixes` (List of String) Canonical CIDR prefixes, all of the rule's `family`.
- `self` (Boolean) Every address of the firewall itself: `self` in pf. Defaults to `false`.
- `table` (String) A table, `<table>` in pf: one pfapid manages (`policy.tables`) or one the base ruleset owns (`policy.ref_tables`, e.g. a `const` table).

<a id="nestedatt--rules--to--ports"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.to.ports`

Required:

- `from` (Number) Port, or first port of a range.

Optional:

- `to` (Number) Last port of the range (inclusive). Omit for a single port.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import pf_qos.fw qos
```
